# Parser fixtures

`traffic.log`, `url.log`, `system.log`, and configuration fixtures are constructed standard-format examples based on the official field references.

`pa1410-12.1-traffic.log` and `pa1410-12.1-dns.log` derive their field count/order and native family/subtype from actual PA-1410 PAN-OS 12.1.4-h8 Syslog captures. The native layouts contain 130 and 140 fields, respectively. **Every customer-identifying value was replaced or cleared**, including all original timestamps, addresses, usernames, rule names, serials, interfaces, URLs, threat identifiers, hostnames, UUIDs, and unknown trailing fields. Public protocol/application/action/subtype/category tokens remain to preserve interpretation. Counts, ports, session IDs, and other numerical values are fixed test data. Original captures are not in this repository.

Four additional 140-field layouts come from independently matched native/stored events: `pa1410-12.1-ml-virus-reset-both.log`, `pa1410-12.1-file-alert.log`, `pa1410-12.1-file-deny.log`, and `pa1410-12.1-wildfire-allow.log`. They cover a non-DNS Threat detection, permitted/denied File Blocking records classified as Data Filtering, and a historical benign WildFire submission. These are separate from `wildfire-virus` Threat detections; File Blocking coverage does not establish native `data` or `dlp` coverage.

The additional fixtures were built from blank arrays with the original field count. Only explicitly allowed public wire, subtype, application, protocol, action, category, severity, direction, file-type, and threat-category tokens were retained. Every other value was replaced with fixed test data or cleared, including all 32 unknown trailing fields. The digest, detection identifier, quoted rule/filename, addresses, timestamps, usernames, and identifiers are synthetic replacements. Original captures and private comparison records are not in this repository.

Tests assert addresses, ports, application, action, subtype/category, verdict/severity, file metadata, timestamps and offsets, byte/packet counters, and extension tolerance. Separate private validation compared actual stored values against matching firewall XML API log sequences. These fixtures establish reproducible parser coverage; they do not establish a fresh WildFire submission or complete transport, UI/export, or appliance acceptance. See `docs/validation/PALO_REAL.md`.

The `constructed-globalprotect-*.log` and `constructed-decryption-*.log` fixtures follow the official [GlobalProtect](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/administration/monitoring/use-syslog-for-monitoring/syslog-field-descriptions/globalprotect-log-fields) and [Decryption](https://docs.paloaltonetworks.com/ngfw/administration/monitoring/use-syslog-for-monitoring/syslog-field-descriptions/decryption-log-fields) default Syslog lists, checked on 2026-10-16: 50 and 107 documented fields, respectively, plus two synthetic extension fields. Every value is constructed test data. They cover successful/failed outcomes, IPv4/IPv6, quoted text, full-width certificate/handshake fields, timestamps, and maximum uint64 identifiers. GlobalProtect event status is exposed through the existing `action` field. Documented fields without a named mapping remain available as `csv_NNN` values; trailing values also remain in `ExtraFields`.

These constructed fixtures do not establish native PAN-OS version compatibility. In particular, release notes mention newer Decryption status fields without providing their offsets in the default CSV list; these fixtures do not guess those offsets. Full native captures and transport/API/UI/export checks remain separate validation requirements.

The eleven `constructed-hip-*`, `constructed-iptag-*`, `constructed-userid-*`, and `constructed-authentication-*` fixtures cover the published default HIP-MATCH (32 fields), IP-Tag (27), User-ID (37), and Authentication (47) layouts, each with two appended unknown fields. Their literal expected values and official reference links are in `constructed-identity-expected.json`. These are constructed examples, not captures from a specific PAN-OS release. IP-Tag event names, HIP type values, and Authentication results are synthetic test values; User-ID cases use the documented login/logout/register-tag/unregister-tag subtypes.

Tests cover all currently named fields, raw CSV positions, ordered trailing fields, normalized values, timestamps, envelopes, core-length boundaries, and the fields that currently have typed validation. Sequence/repeat/timeout/factor values and MAC addresses remain strings; these tests do not claim semantic validation of them. Authentication's string Session ID at index 45 remains available in raw fields and `ExtraFields`, rather than being coerced to the numeric Traffic session ID.

HIP tests distinguish an empty IPv4 field (IPv6 fallback), a valid IPv4/IPv6 pair (IPv4 precedence), and `0.0.0.0` with IPv6 (the current parser retains `0.0.0.0`). The public field definitions do not establish an absent-IPv4 sentinel convention, so this records current behavior without asserting native sentinel semantics. Native capture comparison and transport/API/UI/export acceptance remain separate requirements.
